about.bioTitle: Engineering at the intersection of architectural rigor and intuitive design.
bioParagraphs: Over the past decade, I have focused on building distributed systems that scale predictably and user interfaces that feel instantaneous. My work spans low-latency event-driven backends, WebGL visualization pipelines, and comprehensive enterprise design languages.

I believe the best software products emerge when deep systems infrastructure meets unapologetic attention to typographic nuance, kinetic feedback, and human ergonomics. When not in code, you can find me restoring analog synthesis hardware and mentoring open-source contributors.

blog.title: Practical Consensus: Surviving Split-Brain in Hybrid Clouds
blog.excerpt: Lessons learned implementing the Raft protocol across multi-region cloud providers with asymmetric network partitions.
blog.content:
### Consensus When Networks Are Hostile

Distributed consensus sounds simple in academic papers: majority quorum wins, leader commits entries, followers replicate state. But in multi-cloud production setups, network partitions rarely manifest as clean binary failures.

Instead, you encounter asymmetric latency spikes, flapping TCP keep-alives, and unidirectional packet drops where node A can send to node B, but B cannot respond to A.

#### 1. Pre-Vote Phases Prevent Disruption
Standard Raft triggers election timeouts whenever heartbeats are missed. If a partitioned follower repeatedly starts elections and increments its term number, rejoining the cluster can force an otherwise healthy leader to step down. Implementing the Raft **Pre-Vote** algorithm resolves this by ensuring candidates only advance terms if a quorum of peers confirms they would vote for them.

#### 2. Leased Read Quorums
To sustain 50,000 reads/sec without routing every query through the Raft log, leader leases combined with monotonic clocks guarantee linearizable reads without incurring disk fsync overhead on read paths.

blog.title: Design Tokens Beyond CSS: Generating Multi-Platform Contracts
blog.excerpt: Automating the transformation of Figma semantic variables into type-safe CSS custom properties, Tailwind plugins, and Kotlin Compose themes.
blog.content:
### The Single Source of Truth for Visual Design

A design token is more than a hex code; it is an architectural contract between design intentions and production user experiences.

When designing the Nova system, we automated our token pipeline so that any change committed in Figma automatically triggers a GitHub Actions pipeline that verifies contrast ratios against WCAG 2.2 criteria, generates strict TypeScript types, and publishes immutable versioned npm packages.

testimonials.content: Elena Vance is one of the rarest software engineers in the industry: an architect who can design distributed Raft consensus clusters and simultaneously craft an exquisite, micro-animated user interface with sub-millisecond responsiveness. Her work directly enabled our Series B launch.

Elena audited our streaming architecture and eliminated our persistent p99 latency spikes in less than three weeks. Her deep understanding of system internals and clean API contracts made her an indispensable advisor to our principal staff.

Working with Elena on the Nova design system set a new benchmark for how our engineering and design teams collaborate. The precision of her typography, accessibility standards, and token automation saved our team hundreds of hours.

faq.question: What types of consulting and advisory projects do you take on?
faq.answer: I primarily partner with ambitious technical startups and scale-ups on high-throughput backend architecture, real-time distributed telemetry, and enterprise design systems. Engagements typically range from 2-week architectural deep audits to 6-month fractional staff advisory retainers.

faq.question: How do you approach performance and latency optimization in web applications?
faq.answer: I adhere to a measurement-first philosophy. We profile GC allocations, main-thread blocking times, WebGL draw calls, and network waterfalls before touching a line of code. Solutions often involve moving CPU-intensive parsing to Web Workers, using zero-copy ArrayBuffers, and optimizing CSS token delivery.

faq.question: Are you available for international keynote speaking and technical workshops?
faq.answer: Yes. I regularly speak at international distributed systems and design engineering conferences on topics including consensus safety invariants, WebGL canvas performance, and high-velocity design token pipelines.

faq.question: What is your preferred technology stack for greenfield projects?
faq.answer: For distributed backend systems: Go, Node.js/TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Redis Streams, and Kubernetes. For reactive frontends: TypeScript, React 19, Tailwind CSS, Vite, and Web Audio/WebGL when spatial visualization is required.
